climate.overview_html: The defining new climate signal on September 3 is the direct link between the Super El Niño’s record sea surface temperatures and Hurricane Lowell’s explosive escalation to Category 5 (160 mph) — only the seventh storm ever to reach that threshold in the Central Pacific’s recorded history and the first since Hurricane Walaka in 2018 — with CPHC now warning of a sharp northward track turn that could bring a major hurricane dangerously close to Hawaii early next week. The same El Niño thermodynamic fuel underwrites the catastrophic Nepal–Tibet glacier collapse flood of August 27 — one of the largest glacial lake outburst flood events in Himalayan history, killing more than 1,000 people and leaving 3,000+ missing; climate scientists link this directly to the accelerated glacier melt documented by ICIMOD’s HKH Glacier Outlook 2026, which records a 12% glacial area loss in the Hindu Kush Himalayan region between 1990 and 2020, with 47 Nepalese glacial lakes now classified as potentially dangerous. The European theatre remains unchanged: JRC EFFIS wildfire burnt area tracks 33% above the same date in the record 2025 season with very-extreme fire danger persisting across Romania and Hungary through at least September 5, and NOAA CPC’s August ENSO Diagnostic — still the authoritative reference — assigns >90% probability to a “very strong” El Niño at the September–November peak with all 15 coupled model ensemble members projecting Níño 3.4 above +2.5°C and a majority projecting the +3.0°C “Super El Niño” threshold.

items.headline: NOAA August ENSO Diagnostic: Niño 3.4 Reaches +2.7°C Week of August 12; 15 Ensemble Members Forecast Peak >+3.0°C (“Super El Niño” Threshold); >90% Probability “Very Strong” Event Sept–Nov 2026; No La Niña Transition Before Spring 2027
items.summary: NOAA CPC's August 2026 ENSO Diagnostic Discussion confirms the ongoing El Niño is now tracking toward historically extreme territory. The Niño 3.4 sea surface temperature anomaly index reached +2.03°C in July 2026 and +2.7°C in the week centered on August 12 — already exceeding the +2.5°C threshold for a "very strong" event. All 15 coupled model ensemble members in the multi-model objective ENSO outlook forecast Niño 3.4 exceeding +2.5°C at the September–November peak window; a majority project exceedance of +3.0°C, which would formally qualify this as a "Super El Niño" comparable to the 2015–16 event. NOAA assigns greater than 90% probability to a very strong event during September–November 2026 with little indication of a transition away from El Niño before spring 2027. This ENSO context explains the record global SST of 21.1°C recorded August 22, the hyperactive Pacific season, and the elevated baseline for Northern Hemisphere extreme heat and glacial instability globally.

items.headline: WWA Attribution: European 2026 Summer Heat and Drought Would Have Been Virtually Impossible Without Climate Change — 2.5°C Anthropogenic Amplification; Droughts Now More Severe and More Frequent
items.summary: World Weather Attribution's rapid attribution analysis of the summer 2026 European heat and drought concludes that the observed temperature anomalies and rainfall deficits would have been virtually impossible in a pre-industrial climate. Anthropogenic climate change increased temperatures across the affected region by approximately 2.5°C above a pre-industrial summer baseline. The study finds European droughts are becoming both more severe and more frequent, with soil moisture deficits in 2026 reaching levels not previously observed in the instrumental record across parts of central and southern Europe. The findings directly underpin the Chatham House security assessment and support JRC EFFIS data showing European wildfires in 2026 tracking 33% ahead of the previous record year.

items.headline: Climate Change Is Now Europe’s Biggest Systemic Security Threat — 10,000 Excess Deaths From June Heatwave; 9M Tonnes Crop Loss; Military Assets Diverted to Fire Suppression and Flood Defense
items.summary: Chatham House published a policy analysis concluding that climate change is now Europe's biggest systemic security risk. The summer of 2026 provides the evidence base: extreme heat contributed to an estimated 10,000 excess deaths during the June heatwave alone and destroyed approximately 9 million tonnes of crops. The security dimension is direct: Europe's armed forces are increasingly deployed to fight fires, reinforce flood defenses, evacuate populations, and restore critical infrastructure — diverting capacity from conventional security operations. Rhine water levels fell to their lowest since 1880. Chatham House argues that climate adaptation investment has structurally lagged behind mitigation spending and that European security planning must treat climate hazard as a primary threat category.

items.headline: EU Wildfires 2026: 634,473 Hectares Burned — 33% Above Same Date in Record 2025 Season; Very-Extreme Fire Danger Through September 5; Rhine at Lowest Since 1880; Danube at Record Low; Paks Nuclear Output Curtailed
items.summary: JRC EFFIS reports EU-wide burnt area reached 634,473 hectares as of August 30 — tracking 33% ahead of the same date in the record 2025 season. Very-extreme fire danger indices persist across a broad band running through Romania and Hungary; extreme danger extends to southern Ireland and central-southern Italy through September 5. The Rhine has fallen to its lowest level since 1880, forcing cargo vessels to carry fractional loads. The Danube north of Budapest is at record-low stage; Hungary's Paks Nuclear Power Plant continues curtailing output due to cooling-water temperature exceedances. The atmospheric blocking pattern sustaining the Eastern European heat anomaly shows no credible breakdown signal through September 5.

items.headline: Nepal–Tibet Glacier Collapse Is Climate Crisis in Action: ICIMOD HKH Outlook 2026 Documents 12% Glacial Area Loss 1990–2020; 47 Nepalese Glacial Lakes Classified Dangerous; Scientists Warn Cascading Himalayan GLOF Hazards Inevitable Under Continued Warming
items.summary: Scientists responding to the August 27 Nepal-Tibet catastrophe framed it as an inevitable consequence of accelerating Himalayan glacier loss driven by anthropogenic warming. ICIMOD's HKH Glacier Outlook 2026 documents a 12% loss of glacial area in the Hindu Kush Himalayan region between 1990 and 2020, with ice loss rates accelerating markedly since 2000. Of Nepal's glacial lakes, 47 are currently classified as potentially dangerous; Nepal has experienced 26 confirmed GLOF events since the 1970s, and the trajectory under continued warming projects increasing frequency and intensity of such events. The Tibetan glacial lake drainage identified as the August 27 trigger mechanism is consistent with the pattern of warming-driven lake expansion and instability documented across the high mountain cryosphere. Economic losses from a single major GLOF event can exceed $100 million; the August 2026 disaster — 1,000+ dead, 3,000+ missing, 12 hydropower projects destroyed, entire villages buried — represents a new benchmark for GLOF consequences.

major_events.name: Hurricane Lowell (Central Pacific) — STATUS CHANGE: Escalated to Category 5 (160 mph); Only 7th Central Pacific Cat 5 in Recorded History; First Since Walaka 2018; CPHC Warns Sharp Northward Turn Could Threaten Hawaii Early Next Week; Kauai in Forecast Uncertainty Cone; Honolulu Mayor Issues Preparedness Guidance
major_events.status: CATEGORY 5 · 160 MPH · CPHC NORTH-TURN WARNING · KAUAI RISK EARLY NEXT WEEK · HONOLULU PREP GUIDANCE ISSUED
major_events.impact: Hurricane Lowell underwent one of the most extraordinary rapid intensification sequences in Central Pacific history, surging from 70 mph to 160 mph maximum sustained winds in just over 30 hours — the equivalent of a Category 1-to-5 jump inside a single day. As of the latest CPHC advisories, Lowell is centered approximately 445 miles south of Hilo, moving west near 10 mph, and is now only the seventh hurricane ever to reach Category 5 in the Central Pacific and the first since Hurricane Walaka in 2018. The critical new development: CPHC is warning of a likely sharp turn toward the north or north-northeast late this weekend into early next week, with long-range model guidance progressively shifting the track eastward. Some of the latest ensemble members bring Lowell's center dangerously close to Kauai early next week; the European and Google DeepMind models show a path just west of the islands. The degree of northward turn and its timing introduce significant forecast uncertainty across the island chain. Life-threatening surf and rip currents from Lowell are already spreading northward toward Hawaii. Honolulu Mayor Rick Blangiardi has asked Oahu residents to prepare now. This threat environment exists simultaneously with Hurricane Karina (Cat 4, converging) and Tropical Storm Marie (intensifying) — three active Pacific systems under Super El Niño sea surface temperatures.

major_events.name: Nepal–Tibet Glacier Collapse Floods — NEW: 1,000+ Dead, 3,000+ Missing Including 90 American Nationals; Unstable Barrier Lake at Nepal–China Border Threatens Secondary GLOF; 900+ Workers Unaccounted-For Inside Flooded Hydropower Tunnels; 12 Hydropower Projects Destroyed
major_events.status: 1,000+ DEAD · 3,000+ MISSING · 90 AMERICANS MISSING · BARRIER LAKE RISK · 900+ IN TUNNELS · NEW MAJOR EVENT
major_events.impact: The August 27 glacial collapse event at the Nepal-China border has produced one of the most catastrophic natural disasters in Himalayan history. A bedrock collapse beneath a glacier in the Langtang Lirung area registered as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event, sending a surge of ice, water, rock, and mud down river valleys, burying entire villages and destroying roads, bridges, and critical hydropower infrastructure across Nepal's Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts. As of September 1, the confirmed death toll has passed 1,000 across Nepal and China's Tibet Autonomous Region, with more than 3,000 remaining missing — more than half of them foreign nationals, including at least 90 American citizens according to the US State Department. At least 900 workers are unaccounted-for at 12 damaged hydropower project sites; joint rescue teams have found tunnels either completely buried, blocked, or impossible to enter. A newly-formed unstable barrier lake straddling the Nepal-China border has both governments warning of a secondary catastrophic flood if the dam fails. The Tibetan glacial lake drainage mechanism has been identified by climate bodies as the trigger, consistent with accelerating glacial instability in the high Hindu Kush Himalayan region.

major_events.name: Hurricane Karina (Eastern / Central Pacific) — Cat 4 (140 mph); Entering Central Pacific Late Thursday; Converging Track With Lowell; No Landfall Expected; Combined Hawaii Threat Window With Lowell
major_events.status: CATEGORY 4 · 140 MPH · ENTERING CENTRAL PACIFIC · CONVERGING WITH LOWELL · NO LANDFALL FORECAST
major_events.impact: Hurricane Karina remains a Category 4 major hurricane with maximum sustained winds near 140 mph as of the latest advisories — tracking slightly stronger than September 2 reports of 130 mph. Moving west-northwest, Karina is forecast to enter the Central Pacific basin late Thursday night into Friday on a trajectory that may converge with Lowell's wake in the vicinity of the Hawaiian Islands. NHC forecasts gradual weakening over cooler waters, but Karina is expected to remain a significant hurricane through the Hawaii-region passage window. No landfall is forecast, but the dual-storm configuration simultaneously approaching Hawaii under Super El Niño sea surface temperatures remains historically extraordinary.

major_events.name: Tropical Storm Marie (Eastern Pacific) — 13th Named EP Storm of 2026; Large 160-NM Wind Field; Forecast Hurricane by Wednesday; Three Simultaneous Pacific Systems Under Super El Niño
major_events.status: TROPICAL STORM · INTENSIFYING · FORECAST HURRICANE WED · LARGE WIND FIELD 160 NM RADIUS
major_events.impact: Tropical Storm Marie, the 13th named storm of the 2026 Eastern Pacific hurricane season, continues developing with maximum sustained winds near 45 mph. The storm has an unusually large wind field — tropical storm-force winds extending outward up to 160 nautical miles over the eastern semicircle. NHC projects intensification to hurricane status by Wednesday before Marie encounters drier air and cooler waters. Marie's presence maintains the extraordinary situation of three simultaneous active Pacific systems — Karina (Cat 4), Lowell (Cat 5), and Marie (Tropical Storm) — driven by Super El Niño sea surface temperature anomalies.

Dallas logged 27 days at or above 100°F in August 2026. Severe convective threats along the ridge periphery continue for the Great Lakes and Northeast.

renewables.overview_html: Australia entered the offshore wind era on August 25–26 as Victoria launched the country’s first offshore wind auction — tendering 2 GW across two Bass Strait and Southern Ocean zones, with contracts expected in 2028 and a pathway to 9 GW by 2040. In the US, the structural story remains decisive: EIA data show solar, wind, and storage added 44,889 MW in the year to June 2026 versus only 7,530 MW for natural gas, with combined renewable installed capacity on pace to surpass the entire gas fleet within ≈12 months; California’s lawsuit over the $120M buyout of the 2 GW Golden State Wind lease illustrates the federal–state collision, while wind and solar already hit a record 22.3% share of US electrical production in H1 2026 with solar leading monthly generation for the first time ever in June. In the UK, plug-in residential solar panels became legal under SI 2026/848 from August 27, available at 800+ Argos stores.

items.headline: Victoria Launches Australia’s First Offshore Wind Auction: 2 GW Tendered Across Bass Strait and Southern Ocean Zones; 12-Month RFP Phase; Contracts Expected 2028; Pathway to 9 GW by 2040
items.summary: Victoria launched Australia's first offshore wind auction on August 25–26, opening a 12-month Request for Proposal phase for projects to deliver 2 GW of offshore wind generation. The auction covers two declared offshore wind zones in the Bass Strait off Gippsland and the Southern Ocean off western Victoria. Contracts for the first 2 GW are expected to be awarded in 2028. The 2 GW round is the first step toward Victoria's 4 GW by 2035 and 9 GW by 2040 targets. Successful projects would generate electricity for approximately 1.5 million homes. The auction launch confirms Australia is now operationalizing offshore wind policy after years of legislative development, positioning Victoria as the lead Australian jurisdiction for commercial offshore wind deployment.

items.headline: California Sues Trump Administration Over $120 Million Deal to Cancel 2 GW Golden State Wind Offshore Lease; Alleges Violations of Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act; $100M in Port/Transmission Prep Already Spent
items.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta and the California Energy Commission filed suit August 28 against the Trump administration and Golden State Wind, challenging the Interior Department's April 2026 agreement to pay Golden State Wind $120 million to abandon its 2 GW offshore wind lease and invest instead in fossil fuel projects. The complaint alleges violations of the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act, the Judgment Fund Act, and other federal statutes. The 2 GW project would have supplied clean electricity to more than 1 million California homes. The state notes it has already spent more than $100 million on port upgrades, transmission improvements, and other infrastructure in preparation for the project.

items.headline: EIA Data: US Renewables Installed Capacity to Surpass Natural Gas Within 12 Months — Solar+Wind Added 44,889 MW vs. Gas’s 7,530 MW in Year to June 2026; Battery Storage Up 17,859 MW
items.summary: New EIA capacity data analyzed by Electrek show US renewable energy installed capacity is on pace to surpass natural gas within approximately 12 months — most likely by summer 2027. In the year through June 30, 2026: utility-scale solar added 28,077 MW; small-scale solar added 6,492 MW; wind added 10,553 MW; combined renewable additions totaled 44,889 MW. Natural gas capacity grew by only 7,530 MW in the same period. Utility-scale battery storage added 17,859 MW. When combined renewables capacity eventually exceeds natural gas's installed base, it will mark a structural inflection in the US power system, though natural gas will continue to provide dispatchability that capacity figures alone do not capture.

items.headline: CleanTechnica Analysis: Solar Leads US Monthly Generation for First Time in June 2026; 22.3% of H1 US Production; Renewable Buildout Outpacing Federal Headwinds
items.summary: CleanTechnica's analysis of EIA data concludes that neither Trump administration policy, tariff uncertainty, nor offshore wind cancellations have materially slowed the US solar-wind-storage deployment trajectory. Between July 2025 and June 2026: utility-scale solar grew 28,076.7 MW; small-scale solar added 6,492 MW; wind grew 10,552.9 MW. Combined solar and wind provided 22.3% of domestic electrical production in H1 2026. In June 2026, solar-generated electricity exceeded both wind and hydropower output for the month — the first time solar ranked as the leading renewable source for any single calendar month in US history. The analysis frames federal headwinds as causing friction at the margins rather than reversing structural momentum.

items.headline: UK Plug-In Solar Panels Legal Across Great Britain From August 27 — SI 2026/848 Enables 800 W Residential Systems Via Standard Sockets; Available at 800+ Argos Stores; Saves Up to £110/Year
items.summary: Plug-in solar panels became legal for residential use across England, Wales, and Scotland from August 27, 2026, under Plug-In Solar Amendment SI 2026/848. The regulation allows compliant systems with a maximum rated AC output of 800 W (micro-inverter limited) and combined panel rating up to 2,000 W DC to connect to a home's electricity supply via an approved standard plug and socket, without requiring planning permission or a certified electrician. The change creates a legal pathway that has existed in Germany, France, and the Netherlands for several years but was previously unavailable in the UK. The government estimates systems can save households up to £110 per year; systems are immediately available at over 800 Argos stores across Great Britain.

science.overview_html: The freshest arXiv result in the rolling window is arXiv 2608.30795 (August 31), which renders the Aardvark Weather end-to-end forecasting system probabilistic by attaching learned, input-dependent noise at the observation encoder (aleatoric uncertainty from the observing system) and Monte Carlo dropout in the processor (epistemic uncertainty in learned dynamics); the key payoff is that probabilistic fine-tuning also improves the mean forecast by 4.2% across variables and lead times — uncertainty decomposition and mean-forecast skill turn out to be mutually reinforcing. Newly in the window from outside the ML literature: a Geophysical Research Letters study published August 29 detected 245 previously uncatalogued glacial earthquake events at Thwaites Glacier’s marine edge — most likely capsizing-iceberg impacts — with the busiest cluster in 2018–2020 coinciding precisely with an episodic acceleration of the glacier’s floating ice tongue toward the sea, directly relevant as the Nepal–Tibet GLOF disaster unfolds. Three papers from the mid-window remain active reference: the “Missing the Butterfly” analysis tracing AIWP’s absent butterfly effect to training-data coarse-graining; NOAA’s Nested-EAGLE, which outperforms both GFS and HRRR for near-surface fields over CONUS in a unified short-and-medium-range architecture; and ECMWF’s AIFL LSTM streamflow model, deployed operationally in Copernicus EMS with the ability to detect a 20-year return-level flood signal six days in advance — directly relevant as Pakistan, Nepal, and Southeast Asia face concurrent monsoon, GLOF, and wildfire-haze emergencies.

items.headline: arXiv 2608.30795: Uncertainty-Aware End-to-End AI Weather Forecasting — Aardvark Weather Made Probabilistic; Aleatoric (Observing System) and Epistemic (Model) Uncertainty Decomposed; Probabilistic Fine-Tuning Improves Mean Forecast 4.2%; Law-of-Total-Variance Attribution
items.meta: Almeida, Otero, Arndt, Baur, Samek, Ma · arXiv:2608.30795 · Submitted 31 Aug 2026
items.summary: This paper addresses a critical gap in end-to-end AI weather prediction: Aardvark Weather produces skillful global gridded and station forecasts directly from raw Earth observations, but the system is deterministic. The authors render it probabilistic by attaching two stochastic mechanisms: (1) learned, input-dependent noise at the observation encoder, capturing aleatoric uncertainty inherited from the observing system; and (2) Monte Carlo dropout in the processor, capturing epistemic uncertainty in learned atmospheric dynamics. The resulting nested ensemble attributes forecast spread to the two sources through a law-of-total-variance decomposition. Key empirical result: probabilistic fine-tuning significantly improves the mean forecast by 4.2% on average across variables and lead times — suggesting that uncertainty decomposition and mean-forecast skill are mutually reinforcing rather than in tension. The paper frames the decomposition as essential infrastructure for operational AI weather prediction, where decision-making requires calibrated confidence bounds.

items.headline: GRL: 245 Glacial Earthquakes Detected at Thwaites “Doomsday Glacier” Marine Edge 2010–2023 — Capsizing Iceberg Impacts; Busiest Cluster in 2018–2020 Coincided With Episodic Glacier Acceleration; Signals Destabilizing Ice Dynamics
items.meta: Pham et al. (Australian National University) · Geophysical Research Letters · Published 29 Aug 2026
items.summary: A study published in Geophysical Research Letters (press release August 29, 2026) presents the first systematic detection of 245 previously uncatalogued seismic events near the marine edge of Antarctica's Thwaites Glacier, catalogued over 2010–2023. Out of 362 total Antarctic events detected, 245 (approximately two-thirds) are located near Thwaites' ocean-terminating end. Most are likely glacial earthquakes caused when icebergs calve, capsize, and collide violently with the parent glacier — a mechanism that generates seismic waves propagating thousands of kilometers. Critically, the busiest cluster of events occurred during 2018–2020, a period that coincided with episodic acceleration of Thwaites' floating ice tongue toward the sea as observed in satellite data. This correlation suggests that changing ocean conditions destabilizing the ice may simultaneously drive both faster glacier flow and more calving activity. The findings add seismic evidence to the broader body of research showing Thwaites' marine-based instability is accelerating, with direct implications for global sea level projections.

items.headline: arXiv 2608.25835: AI Weather Models “Missing the Butterfly” and Skillful Backcasting Traced to Training-Data Coarse-Graining — Physics-Like Properties Recoverable by Reducing Coarse-Graining; Implication for Benchmark Accuracy Claims
items.summary: A paper from the LMU Munich/ECMWF group identifies a unified root cause for two puzzling behaviors of AI weather prediction models: their failure to simulate the butterfly effect (sensitivity to initial-condition perturbations — a fundamental property of atmospheric chaos) and their surprising ability to skillfully backcast. The explanation: training data coarse-graining removes fast, small-scale modes, creating a temporally smoothed training distribution in which the model learns to interpolate rather than model true atmospheric dynamics. When coarse-graining is progressively reduced, the arrow of time and butterfly-effect sensitivity re-emerge. The finding has direct consequence for how AIWP benchmark accuracy should be interpreted: some of the accuracy advantage attributed to neural weather models may reflect temporal smoothing rather than genuine dynamical skill.

items.headline: arXiv 2608.26822 (Nested-EAGLE): Single ML System Bridges 0.25° Global and 6-km Regional Forecasting Over CONUS; Lower MSE Than Both GFS and HRRR for Near-Surface Fields; Unified Short- and Medium-Range Architecture
items.summary: A NOAA team introduces Nested-EAGLE, an ML weather prediction system that unifies short-range and medium-range forecasting in a single architecture. Nested-EAGLE combines a 0.25° global forecast model with a 6 km refinement over CONUS, incorporating high-resolution regional analysis data into training through the nesting process. Key result: Nested-EAGLE achieves significantly lower mean-squared error in near-surface and low-level quantities over CONUS compared to both GFS and HRRR, while remaining competitive globally. The authors argue that unifying short- and medium-range prediction into a single coherent system would provide the public with an improved distillation of global weather and local impacts, replacing NOAA's current multi-system approach.

items.headline: ECMWF Operationally Deploys AIFL: LSTM Global Streamflow Model Trained on 18,588 Basins; Detects 20-Year Flood Signal 6 Days in Advance; Enters Copernicus EMS Flood Service
items.summary: ECMWF announced the operational deployment of AIFL (AI for Floods) on August 27, 2026 within the Copernicus Emergency Management Service global flood forecasting component. AIFL is a deterministic LSTM trained on 18,588 river basins from the CARAVAN dataset using a two-stage approach: pre-training on 40 years of ERA5-Land reanalysis, then fine-tuned on IFS control forecasts. Independent test performance (2021–2024): median modified KGE′ of 0.66 and median NSE of 0.53 globally. Most operationally significant: AIFL detected a 20-year return-level flood signal six days in advance during the January 2024 Storm Henk floods in Belgium. The deployment is directly relevant to ongoing flood emergencies in Pakistan, Nepal, and the Philippines, and underscores the operational stakes of GLOF-capable early warning.

items.title: Verisk 2026 Global Modeled Catastrophe Losses Report: Industry Should Prepare for $171 Billion in Average Annual Insured Losses — Up $19 Billion Year-on-Year; US Accounts for $117B (68%) of Global AAL; 100-Year Loss at $477B; Highest Estimate Verisk Has Ever Reported
items.body_html: Verisk released its 2026 Global Modeled Catastrophe Losses Report on September 1, calculating that the insurance industry should be prepared to absorb $171 billion in insured catastrophe losses on an average annual basis — up $19 billion from its prior-year estimate and the highest average annual loss (AAL) figure Verisk has ever published. Of the $171 billion global insured AAL, $117 billion (68%) is attributed to the United States; the 100-year return-period scenario yields $477 billion in aggregate insured losses, and the 250-year scenario reaches $606 billion. A companion release covers Europe: Europe carries $110 billion in expected annual economic catastrophe losses, of which only about $24 billion is currently insured — a protection gap of roughly 78%. The benchmark rose even after a year without a US hurricane landfall for the first time in a decade, reflecting continued growth in property values and insured exposure in coastal and wildfire-prone areas. The 2026 European wildfire and drought season, plus the potential Hawaii landfall of Hurricane Lowell, could contribute to upward revisions in subsequent editions.
items.source_html: GlobeNewswire / Verisk / Insurance Journal

items.title: RFC Power Closes £10 Million Series A and Rebrands as Certain Energy — British Business Bank Leads; Centrica Energy, Ceres Power, and Temasek Trust C3H Participate; Manganese Flow Battery LDES Platform Targets Grid-Scale Deployment
items.body_html: RFC Power, an Imperial College London spin-off developing manganese-electrolyte flow batteries for long-duration energy storage, closed a £10 million ($12.7 million) Series A on August 26 and simultaneously rebranded as Certain Energy. The round was led by the British Business Bank, which contributed £3.5 million, with participation from Centrica Energy, Ceres Power Holdings, and Temasek Trust’s Catalytic Capital for Climate and Health (C3H). Certain Energy’s flow battery uses a manganese electrolyte — the 12th most abundant element in the Earth’s crust — and extends discharge duration by scaling electrolyte tank volume, enabling storage from hours to days without chemistry changes. The company plans to develop a grid-connected MWh-class demonstration system in India, expand its UK research facility, and build a supply chain for replicable utility-scale projects.
items.source_html: Renewable Energy Magazine / Solar Power Portal

items.title: Redstone Closes €25 Million First Tranche of Blue Economy Decarbonization Fund — Targeting Maritime Sector Carbon Reduction, Ocean Asset Security, and Coastal Infrastructure Resilience
items.body_html: Berlin- and Helsinki-based fund manager Redstone closed the first tranche of its blue economy decarbonization fund at €25 million during the week of August 28, targeting investments in technologies to decarbonize maritime sectors, secure ocean-based assets, and build resilient coastal infrastructure. The fund addresses a sector responsible for approximately 2.5% of global greenhouse gas emissions that has historically attracted less climate investment than aviation, trucking, or industrial processes. Alternative fuels (ammonia, methanol, green hydrogen), hull efficiency technologies, and port electrification represent core investment themes. The first close reflects growing investor interest in maritime decarbonization as the IMO’s strengthened 2050 net-zero shipping target creates regulatory pull for clean propulsion and alternative fuel solutions.

items.title: BlocPower Shuts Down and Liquidates — Community Clean Energy Electrification Platform Winds Down After 14 Years; Returns Capital to Investors
items.body_html: BlocPower, the community-focused clean energy company that electrified buildings in low-income urban neighborhoods by replacing gas heating and cooling systems with electric heat pumps and solar, is shutting down and liquidating its assets, returning remaining capital to investors. BlocPower had operated since 2012, achieving significant attention for its mission of decarbonizing community buildings in underserved neighborhoods across New York City and other markets. The shutdown reflects the persistent difficulty of achieving financial sustainability in community-scale energy efficiency retrofit businesses, which face thin margins, complex multi-party project execution, and slow payment cycles. The closure is a notable setback for impact-oriented community climate tech and underscores the structural challenges facing mission-driven platforms trying to deploy clean energy in underserved markets at scale.
